free.title: LAST CHANCE: FRIDA AND DIEGO AT MOMA
free.caption:
LAST CHANCE · MOMA

Two days left to see Frida and Diego together at MoMA, and yes, it's been selling out timed slots all summer.

Frida and Diego: The Last Dream traces their 26-year love story through paintings, photos and archival pieces, staged inside sets built by the Met Opera's own production designer. It closes Saturday, September 12, and the galleries reset right after.

Friday hours run latest (til 8:30pm) if you want to dodge the weekend crowd. General admission is $30 and covers the whole museum, Van Gogh and Monet included.

Send this to whoever still hasn't seen it - there's no second chance on this run.

📷 MoMA

food.title: EATALY FLATIRON
food.caption:
FOOD · FLATIRON

Eataly Flatiron is 50,000 square feet of Italy under one roof, and most New Yorkers still only know the entrance.

Past the front doors: a pasta counter making tagliatelle to order, a wood-fired pizza oven, a full butcher and fish counter, a gelato bar, and Eataly Vino pouring 200+ Italian wines by the glass upstairs. Seven sit-down restaurants are tucked inside if you actually want to sit.

Go before noon if you want first pick at the pasta counter, it's the best seat in the building. Open daily 7am to 11pm, no reservation needed to just walk in and graze.

Tag your go-to lunch crew, this is a whole afternoon.

📷 Eataly NYC

art.title: THE DJANGO AFTER DARK
art.caption:
AFTER DARK · TRIBECA

Most jazz clubs kick you out by midnight. The Django doesn't.

Tucked in the cellar of the Roxy Hotel, this basement room has run live jazz nightly since it opened, red walls, low ceilings, a horseshoe bar built to feel like 1920s Paris. Sets run 'til late most nights, well past when everyone else's kitchen has closed. Cover is $35 Sunday through Thursday, $40 Friday and Saturday, plus a 2-drink minimum.

Doors open 6:30pm (6pm Sunday), but the room really fills up after 9. Thursday through Saturday sell out, so book ahead if you want a table instead of standing room.

Save this for the next time your night needs to run longer.

📷 The Django NYC
